name: radvd
why: IPv6 Router Advertisement daemon is a real door into SLAAC and NDP, the quiet protocol running every IPv6 network.

brief.what_it_is: radvd is the IPv6 Router Advertisement Daemon, a small server run on a Linux or BSD machine acting as an IPv6 router. It listens for Router Solicitation messages and sends Router Advertisement messages (RFC 4861) onto the local LAN, both periodically and when a host asks. Its input is a configuration file (radvd.conf) describing prefixes, lifetimes, DNS options and similar settings for each interface. Its output is the advertisements themselves, which let hosts configure their own addresses and pick a default router. The package also ships radvdump, a companion tool that dumps the Router Advertisements it sees on the wire.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says radvd is run by Linux or BSD systems acting as IPv6 routers and that its messages are required for IPv6 stateless autoconfiguration. The GitHub README adds that hosts can then configure addresses and other parameters automatically and choose a default router from these advertisements.
brief.how_it_works: radvd sends Router Advertisements periodically to the all-routers multicast group and answers Router Solicitations from hosts. Each advertisement carries the options the admin configured, such as prefixes, lifetimes, route information, and DNS (RDNSS and DNSSL) entries. The README's FAQ stresses the design philosophy: radvd only advertises, and it does not assign addresses, configure routes, or run a routing or forwarding daemon. Those jobs are left to the admin or init scripts.

commands_seen.context: Build step from the GitHub README; the example install configuration, with prefix, sysconfdir and mandir set explicitly.
Clones the source repository from the homepage for development or building from source.
Named in the README prose as the step after building: 'Run make and make install'. On BSD the README says you may need gmake instead of make.

brief.install_notes: Build from source: run ./configure (see configure --help for options), then make and make install. On BSD you may need gmake. Release tarballs (tar.gz or tar.xz) come with signatures and sha256/sha512 checksums. Configuration is described in INTRO.html, radvd.conf(8) and radvd.conf.example, which are not reached from the pages I read. The README and CHANGES mention libcheck for the make check test target, but I did not confirm the exact build dependencies. The README does not mention hardware or accounts. Root or the required privileges are needed, since it opens raw ICMPv6 and netlink sockets, but I did not read this in the pages.
brief.standout: It is a single-purpose daemon that deliberately does less than the router-config tools people expect: it advertises prefixes and options but never configures interfaces or addresses. It is also the reference implementation many Linux distributions use for SLAAC and RDNSS, and its changelog goes back to 2001.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage lists release v2.21 dated 2026/05/25, with a changelog covering CVE-2026-48715 in radvdump, and the GitHub README's RFC key is dated 2026/07/04. The maintainer is listed as Robin Hugh Johnson, with previous maintainers named. I did not see a last-commit date.
brief.caveats: The homepage says Linux is supported and BSD mileage may vary. The GitHub README says Secure Neighbor Discovery (SEND) is not implemented at all, and several RFC items are only partial, including RFC 4861 shutdown behaviour and RFC 6775. radvd does not configure addresses, routes, or routing/forwarding, so admins must set those up themselves. The homepage cites RFC 2461 while the GitHub README cites RFC 4861, which is the current spec. The homepage's mailing lists and IRC channel are for development, not support. License not checked.
